page.title: Run review
page.purpose: Let a reviewer judge a conformance run: what each chapter asserted, what it observed, which strategy produced the observation, and whether the evidence can support a release claim at all.

priorities.statement: Each chapter shows expected versus observed, not just pass or fail.
priorities.notes: A reviewer cannot judge a verdict they cannot see the basis for.

priorities.statement: Every chapter names the strategy that produced it and whether that strategy is semantic or pixel-grade.
priorities.notes: The same chapter carries very different weight depending on whether an accessibility tree or OCR produced it.

priorities.statement: A run built from non-promotable evidence says so at the top, not in a footnote.
priorities.notes: A reviewer must not read a green run and assume it can gate a release.

priorities.statement: A bounded policy that was exceeded reads as a failure with its bound, never as a longer wait.
priorities.notes: Silently extending a wait converts a real defect into a slow pass.

states.description: A complete passing run on a simulator via ios-simctl, semantic tier, with a decoded recording.
A run in progress; completed chapters are readable and pending ones are explicitly pending, not blank.
One chapter failed on an assertion. The failing expectation and observation are both visible.
Every chapter passed, but the run was driven by ios-mirror. The run is green and explicitly cannot contribute to a release gate.
Native shell chapters ran; web-content chapters are unavailable because BAS could not attach to the WKWebView. The run reports partial honestly rather than passing.

claims.statement: Every asserted chapter displays both its expected value and its observed value.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-006. A verdict without its basis cannot be reviewed, only trusted.

claims.statement: Every chapter names its executing strategy and capability tier.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-005. A semantic assertion and an OCR match are different kinds of evidence and must never be presented identically.

claims.statement: A run whose evidence cannot gate a release states that before any chapter detail, and the statement is legible in text without colour.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-010. A green non-promotable run is the most dangerous artifact this scenario can produce, because it looks exactly like a releasable one.

claims.statement: A chapter whose readiness or settle bound was exceeded reads as failed and displays the bound it exceeded.
claims.rationale: Bounded policies exist so slowness is a signal. Presenting an exceeded bound as anything else destroys that signal.
